skill.name: star-story-extraction
skill.description: Extracts completed work into concise STAR interview stories with situation, task, action, result, and interview variations.
skill.summary: Turns completed technical work into interview-ready STAR stories.
skill.author: DanielPodolsky

content.value_statement: Completed work is hard to turn into clear interview answers. This skill structures achievements as concise STAR stories with technical depth.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the story type for completed technical work.
Guides users through situation, task, action, and result prompts.
Provides a reusable Markdown story template.
Shows examples of weak and strong STAR answers.
Suggests interview question variations for each story.
Recommends saving stories under a career stories folder.
limitations: It does not verify whether metrics are accurate.
It depends on user-provided project context.
It does not conduct live interview practice.
It does not create resumes or cover letters.

use_cases.title: Prepare Behavioral Answers
use_cases.description: Turn a finished project into a focused story for behavioral interviews.

use_cases.title: Capture Work Wins
use_cases.description: Record achievements soon after delivery, while details and metrics are still fresh.

use_cases.title: Coach Junior Developers
use_cases.description: Use guided questions to help juniors describe ownership, decisions, and results.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic STAR Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this completed task: [task]. Ask me for missing context, then draft a STAR story.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Story Depth
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft STAR story: [story]. Strengthen technical actions, ownership, and measurable results.

prompt_templates.title: Map Story to Questions
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this STAR story: [story]. List interview questions it can answer and adapt the wording for each.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Story Portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these project notes: [notes]. Extract three distinct STAR stories and label the strongest interview theme for each.

output_examples.input: Completed a JWT authentication flow with refresh tokens and signup UX improvements.
output_examples.output: A concise STAR story showing the signup problem, the authentication redesign, the security trade-off, and measured conversion gains.

output_examples.input: Fixed a slow reporting query that blocked a release.
output_examples.output: A technical challenge story that explains diagnosis, indexing choices, testing, and the final performance impact.

output_examples.input: Mentored a junior developer through a difficult refactor.
output_examples.output: A leadership story focused on coaching, code quality decisions, risk reduction, and the junior developer's growth.

best_practices: Capture metrics and dates while the project details are fresh.
Use first-person language for actions you personally owned.
Keep each spoken story near two to three minutes.
anti_patterns: Do not invent metrics or claim outcomes you cannot support.
Do not describe only team work without your specific decisions.
Do not include long background that hides the main technical action.

faq.question: What is a STAR story?
faq.answer: It is an interview answer organized by situation, task, action, and result.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after completing a project, fixing a bug, or delivering a meaningful feature.

faq.question: Does it write stories automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structure and prompts, but strong output needs accurate project details from you.

faq.question: Can it help with technical interviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps explain technical choices, trade-offs, and impact in a clear interview format.

faq.question: Does it save files by itself?
faq.answer: No. It suggests a save location, but file creation depends on the host tool.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
